The era of data is coming!

&eThe Nitrogen in the final step of its recipe should be added in the Basin!&r

ftbquests.chapter_111_2.quest_2A72FAB16A:
The impact of the Big Rip has become completely intertwined with this species.

For Ice Dragons, if raised with a targeted approach, the expected resource output from a single dragon egg is essentially fixed.

But just like Creative Filling Tanks, the Big Rip curses the fire dragon species—their cell division possesses an unstoppable chaotic tendency. For Fire Dragons growing naturally, their evolution over millennia has granted them some means of resistance. However, for accelerated-growth Fire Dragons, every cell division is uncontrollable.

As a result, Fire Dragon-related recipes carry a certain randomness and will vary depending on certain factors. Therefore, you cannot produce according to a fixed ratio. &eThe most effective choice is to dynamically send items to the production line based on the inventory of different materials!&r

Fire Dragon Blood is extremely precious—it can be used to proliferate Blue Blaze Chlamydia.

If you produce excess fire dragon blood, you can sell it to me using the Auto-Trading Terminal.
ftbquests.chapter_111_2.quest_2F92310236:
Fire Dragons were dragons from the very beginning—they are a species native to the Nether.

You may have already seen the fossils in the Nether—those are the remains of the Fire Dragons' ancestors. The Big Rip caused all the ancestors of the Fire Dragons that stayed in the Nether to go extinct. Fortunately, a small portion of the Fire Dragons' ancestors were cast into the Overworld by the aftershocks of the Big Rip. Due to the unsuitable environment, the surviving ancestors of the Fire Dragons changed their forms, shrinking their size and lowering their body temperature, successfully taking root in the Overworld, and eventually evolving into the Fire Dragons of today.

They had not yet formed a civilization before the Big Rip—but what difference does that make? In the face of such a catastrophe, the vast majority of civilizations can only face death.

Alright, now let's take a look at how to bring them into production!

&6(Please note that the following content has not been fully verified and lacks key evidence)&r
This might seem counterintuitive, but given the history of Ice Dragons, it wouldn't be surprising if Fire Dragons shared a similar history.

You know, in the Nether, there is a unique civilization—the Piglin civilization. They have an unshakable love for gold ingrained in their bones. Coincidentally, the Fire Dragons are the same; moreover, almost all species in this world that were born before the Big Rip have some kin that have been twisted by it, yet I have not found such kin for the Fire Dragons. In terms of time, the Piglin civilization did emerge around the time of the Big Rip, but unlike other Nether species born after it, they cannot survive in the Overworld—it is as if they are cursed by the Big Rip, unable to truly live there. So I speculate that the Fire Dragons left behind in the Nether may not have truly gone extinct, and may have even developed their own civilization along the way

If we follow this line of thought, then the traits exhibited by Hoglins are quite thought-provoking—they may be products of Fire Dragons mutating in another direction

If this truly is the case, then the fate of the Ice Dragons is truly lamentable
ftbquests.chapter_111_2.quest_617FBB00C4:
I think it's time for me to talk to you more about the Big Rip. To return to your homeworld, you must understand the Big Rip.

You've probably encountered countless times the dragons in their lairs, the Stymphalian Birds in the swamps, the mysterious Ghosts, and the wandering Cyclopes. The first time you see these strange beasts often makes your hair stand on end—but I believe you're past that stage. Let's start with the dragons: Ice Dragons, Fire Dragons, and Lightning Dragons. Although they're quite similar to each other now, in the past, the three types of dragons were actually completely different species, until the arrival of the Big Rip changed everything... Well, you might not be interested in that, so we'll talk about it later.

&aSo now, it's time to think about how to make them a boost to your production!&r

Before you start, you first need to obtain a dragon egg—&eyou can get one by transforming an End Dragon egg, purchasing it from the Grocery, or killing a stage-five dragon to obtain a dragon egg!&r

As a variation, this part isn't mandatory, but it can bring you many practical gains!

Ice Dragons were once a native species of earth, and mutated into what they are today under the influence of the Big Rip—you may have seen their kin mutating in a different direction—&7Strays&r

Before you rush to be surprised, or refute this using the contents of that &eBestiary&r—this civilization is still young, so their records naturally cannot trace back to the distant past.

Although I don't know what your homeworld looks like, I can give you a brief overview of the basic picture of our world — &a"Everything is information".&r

In our world, all material entities can be broken down into the same fundamental unit — information — thus, all material entities are representations of information space. On this basis, everything that happens in the world is the migration and rearrangement of information — and all the laws of the world (such as chunk loading rules, entity stacking rules, etc.) are essentially a special type of information — they can self-replicate and act upon other information, governing its migration and rearrangement.

&eIf we use a computer as an analogy, information space is the world's "storage", material entities are the world's "display", and the laws of the world are the "programs".&r

You might ask: What about the "memory"?

"Memory" is the role played by &dInformation Elements&r.

You may not have encountered it yet — &eInformation Elements are materialized information itself&r — they are both the information itself and its own representation. For the world, they are both material entities and the underlying structure of information space. The world's "programs" can be stored in Information Elements as material entities, and directly influence the underlying structure of information space through them.

In the future, you might be able to use Information Elements to transform matter, create matter, or even modify the laws of the world!

For example, when information is rearranged, two materials with the same amount of information can be transformed into each other.

When using, first press &e[Shift] + Right-click&r to bind to the network.

After equipping the Portable Network Terminal, you can press &a[H]&r to open the Information Storage Network.

Unlike the GUI opened by pressing &a[O]&r, the crafting slots in the GUI opened by pressing &a[H]&r will retain the items inside when closed (in fact, they are temporarily stored in the Portable Network Terminal).

Additionally, a convenient feature is: when you press &a[Shift]&r + &aMiddle-click&r, you can store items held in main-hand into the dimension network!

Network Interfaces are used to automatically replenish items into the Information Storage Network! — However, they cannot be used to extract items.

&aYou can use various logistics tools to place items into it&r, and it will automatically store the items into the network &e(each item type will not exceed 65,536)&r. The arrow-marked slot in its GUI can serve as a blacklist filter for the slot below, but generally, you don't need to do this.

A network interface in popup mode will automatically eject items that do not match the filter into adjacent containers.

When you place a network interface, it will automatically bind to the network you are on.

Only the network manager can use the Network Destructor Charm to destroy the network.

To use it, first press &e[Shift] + Right-click&r to bind it to the network, then hold right-click for five seconds to destroy the network!

When the network is destroyed, all information within it will be reset to its initial state — you will permanently lose all materials stored in it — so you'd better be sure you want to do this!

The Schematic Interface can be used to connect the Schematicannon to the Information Storage Network!

Schematicannons near the Schematic Interface can directly extract required items from the Information Storage Network!

Only the network manager can use the Member Connector to link the network to others.

To use it, first press &eShift + Right-click&r to bind it to the network, then give the bound connector to the other person and right-click it to add them to the network!

Only network manager can use the Network Gifter to gift a network.

To use it, first press &eShift + Right-click&r to bind it to a network. Then, give the bound gifter to the other person and right-click it to gift them the network!

When a network is gifted, all material vectors in your network will be transferred to the recipient's network in batches — any overflow will be reverted to its initial state, and both you and the recipient will permanently lose those materials.
Your Digitize Information Element is lost? The Information Storage Network is damaged? — Just use any Information Element as an exchange!

&aThe Information Storage Network is a storage system that is more suitable for engineering than a backpack.&r

Take this &dDigitize Information Element&r. It can be used to create an Information Storage Network. If your network is damaged, I can provide you with a Digitize Information Element for free — transmitting them is effortless for me, and I still have a large stockpile. You just need to offer any other Information Element in exchange.

&eEach person can only establish a link with one network. If needed, you can use some items to gift, share, share ownership, or destroy a network.&r

When you use a Digitize Information Element to create an Information Storage Network, the Digitize Information Element first dissociates into non-material information. Then, it transforms itself into an "executable world program". The world will automatically execute it, carving out a &eradius 65536, 216-dimensional sphere&r at a specific coordinate in a specific infinite-dimensional information space, and establishes its connection with the physical world. This creates a brand new Information Storage Network. &e(If you don't understand this, just turn to the next page and read the yellow text.)&r

&aWhen materials are stored into the Information Storage Network, they are first converted into corresponding Information Elements, then dissociated into non-physical information and stored as a basis vector within the infinite-dimensional information space where the network resides — the quantity of the material is the magnitude of this vector. &eYou can press [O] anywhere to link to the network and access the materials stored within.&r &aWhen extracting, this basis vector is reassembled into the corresponding Information Element, which is then transformed back into physical materials by the network program.&r

Since the network itself is a radius 65536, 216-dimensional sphere, &ethis means you can store up to 216 types of materials, with a maximum of 65536 units per type.&r

&eIn the future, you can use &dNet Expander Information Elements&r &eto expand the network's dimensionality, thereby increasing the storage type limit.&r

You might wonder: a sphere of radius 65536 in n dimensions, where materials are represented as basis vectors — if the magnitude of a vector represents the quantity of a material, then what does its direction (positive or negative) signify?

Actually, when materials are stored within the network, their corresponding vectors are all positive. That is, in a static state, each vector in the network always lies within the positive hemisphere.

When you remove an item from the network, you are essentially applying a negative material vector to the network. This symmetry break prevents the materials in the network from transmuting (rotation of the basis vector frame) into other materials, as such transmutation could lead to non-conservation of the total information in the network — thus ensuring that the materials in the network do not "transform" into something else.

At the same time, you might be curious: how does the network simultaneously store/withdraw large quantities of multiple materials? (The sum vector of these materials could have a magnitude far greater than 65536.)

In practice, when a vector is applied to the network, the network first decomposes it into a series of basis vectors, which are then merged into the network in batches. This avoids the issue of magnitude overflow!

Balancing this production process involves, finding positive integers k1 and k2 s.t. k1*a = k2*b. In this case, k1*a is a common multiple of a and b.
&eIf k1*a is the LCM of a and b, then k1 and k2 represent the minimum balancing ratio for this production process.&r

&aQuick Calculation Method: &r

&eGiven two positive integers a and b, we can easily know that:&r
lcm(a,b)*gcd(a,b) = a*b

Based on this, we only need to find one of lcm(a,b) or gcd(a,b) to calculate the other. We use prime factorization to quickly find lcm(a,b).

&eConsider the prime factorization of a and b, then compare their prime factors and their exponents, supplementing the missing exponents and prime factors for both sides (TN: if a=Π(pi^ai), b=Π(pi^bi), then lcm(a,b)=Π(pi^max(ai,bi)) ) — due to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, we can be sure this is the LCM!&r

Take 28 and 18 as an example:
28 = 4*7 = 2^2 * 7
18 = 2*9 = 2 * 3^2
&eIt is easy to notice that if lcm(a,b) is divisible by a and b, then lcm(a,b) should be simultaneously divisible by every part of their prime factorizations.&r

-Both have the prime factor 2, but 28 has a higher exponent, so lcm(a,b) should have the factor 2^2 = 4.
-28 does not have the prime factor 3, but 18 does with an exponent of 2, so lcm(a,b) should have the factor 3^2 = 9.
-18 does not have the prime factor 7, but 28 does with an exponent of 1, so lcm(a,b) should have the factor 7.

&eThus, we immediately get lcm(a,b) = 2^2 * 3^2 * 7 = 4*9*7 = 252.&r

When calculating the expected output of cyclic processing (such as draining cap pieces), you may run into some difficulties.

Take the Item Drain processing cap pieces as an example: &a1 cap piece produces 10 mB of Spore each time, with a 25%% chance of being retained (each processing is independent)&r

If you want to calculate the expectation directly, you need to compute an infinite series like this: &e10 * 3/4 * (1 + 2 * 1/4 + 3 * (1/4)^2 + ... )&r

You may lack the necessary knowledge to compute it, so here we'll teach you how to calculate such series in two ways. &a(Don't worry too much about their rigor—after all, if you still need this knowledge, chances are you're not major in math or a mathematician.)&r

&e1. You can understand "each output is 10mB, with a 25%% chance of being retained" as "0.75 Cap Piece = 10mB Spore"&r
So you can easily calculate that 1 Cap Piece = 13.33...mB Spore

&e2. Let's consider a more general case:&r
&a1 + 2 * q + 3 * q^2 + ... = A (0 < q < 1) &r&e①&r
Multiply both sides of ① by q, we get
&aq + 2 * q^2 + 3 * q^3 + ... = q * A &r&e②&r
① - ②, that is
&a1 + q + q^2 + ... = (1 - q) * A &r&e③&r
Then multiply both sides of ③ by q, we get
&aq + q^2 + q^3 + ... = q * (1 - q) * A &r&e④&r
③ - ④, that is
&a1 = (1 - q)^2 * A&r

Thus we get &eA = (1/(1 - q))^2&r
Then we can derive that 1 Cap Piece = 7.5 * (1/(1 - 1/4))^2 = 7.5 * 16/9 = 13.33...mB Spore

Appendix - A Not-So-Strict Proof:
&6Axiom 1:&r&eReal numbers are continuous on the number line&r
&6Definition 1:&r&eFor a sequence {a_n} and a real number a, if for any given ε > 0, there exists an N ∈ N* (the set of natural numbers) such that when n > N, we have&r&a |a_n - a| < ε &r&eThen a is called the limit of {a_n} as n tends to positive infinity, or the sequence {a_n} converges to a, and it is denoted as &r&alim_(n→+∞) a_n = a&r
&6Theorem 1:&r&eWhen two sequences converge, the limit of their arithmetic operations (if meaningful) equals the arithmetic operations of their limits (if meaningful)&r
&6Definition 2:&r&eFor an infinite sequence&r &aa_1, a_2, a_3, ..., a_n, ...&r&e, the expression&r&aa_1 + a_2 + ...&r&e is called an infinite series of constant terms, and a_n is its n-th term&r
&6Definition 3:&r&eIf the sum of the first n terms of an infinite series &aa_1 + a_2 + ... + a_n &r&e is denoted as S_n, and if the sequence formed by S_n has a limit S, then the infinite series is said to converge with sum S, written as &r&aa_1 + a_2 + ... = S&r

For an infinite series &a1 + 2 * q + 3 * q^2 + ... + n * q^(n - 1) + ... (0 < q < 1)&r
its partial sum of the first n terms &aS_n = 1 + q + ... + n * q^(n - 1) = (1 - (n + 1) * q^n + n * q^(n + 1)))/(1 - q)^2&r

We can easily prove that {q^n} converges to 0, and next we prove that {n * q^n} converges to 0.
Let q = 1/(1 + a) (a > -1); then the problem reduces to proving that {n * 1/(1 + a)^n} converges to 0.
Since (1 + a)^n = 1 + a + n * (n + 1)/2 * a + ... > n * (n + 1)/2 * a, we have
n * 1/(1 + a)^n < 2/((n - 1) * a^2).

Thus: for any given ε > 0, let N = floor(1 + 2/(a^2 * ε)) + 1; then when n > N, |n * q^n| < ε, so {n * q^n} converges to 0.

Therefore, by Theorem 1, lim_(n→+∞) S_n = 1/(1 - q)^2.

Q.E.D.

The vast majority of logistics in this modpack are designed to operate completely without logistics mods like AE2 or Create: Ender Transmission.&r

However, due to player requests, LaserIO (along with the Remote Upgrades from the Storage Drawer mod) has been added as an "ultra-simplified solution" for players who don't want to spend too much effort on logistics management. After the release of this modpack, I received many questions about logistics mods such as AE2, LaserIO, RS, etc. — naturally, some discordant voices emerged.

I needs to clarify that the design philosophy of this modpack leans more towards various factory automation games rather than a traditional Minecraft tech pack, so logistics are inevitably a core gameplay element.

&eFor automation games, logistics systems are never about being as convenient as possible!&r The belt system in Factorio is roughly as complex as Create — it even requires knowledge of infinite series for tasks like splitting a belt into three belts with averaged flow. In Shapez, a game where machines don't consume materials but require extensive long-distance logistics, there are no trains, even the blueprints requires consuming blueprint materials. Satisfactory lacks a proper train system (no support for stations with the same name, and train intersections can't fit even the largest tier-3 blueprint), and its splitters are extremely unintelligent...

&eAs an important part of automation gameplay, &r&aunless absolutely necessary&r&e, factory games will not provide overly intelligent logistics methods! &rIf you don't like logistics puzzles and production line design, then colony simulation games like Frostpunk, Banished, or Timberborn, which have no logistics or highly intelligent logistics, are more suitable for you!

For the logistics needs of this modpack, Create's own logistics system, Drawers, and the modpack's custom logistics are already &ecompletely sufficient&r. Mods like AE2, RS, LaserIO, and Create: Ender Transmission would be pure crutches in this modpack.

— Of course, &eusing crutches is a perfectly normal thing&r, so I has also included LaserIO in this modpack by default. However, is it a bit (    ) to mock others who don't use crutches as making trouble for themselves while playing with crutches? &o(Fill in the blank, 5 points)&r

Such disputes are meaningless, and I will no longer respond to related arguments or "suggestions".

Regarding Automation and Intelligence:
In more "tech modpack" terms, it's the difference between passive production lines and on-demand production lines.

In passive production lines, intelligent logistics (such as trains) are at most used to connect factories, and the logistics needs of each machine are relatively fixed. In this case, only a small amount of cache is needed to ensure normal operation, and centralized storage or large-scale storage are meaningless.

In on-demand production lines, intelligent logistics run from the starting point to the endpoint (inside the factory), allowing production to be carried out "on-demand." Under these conditions, logistics needs are highly uncertain and change frequently, requiring a large amount of cache to ensure order efficiency, which leads to the concept of a "central warehouse".

For automation games, at most, they provide high-capacity intelligent logistics at the starting point (such as train systems) and low-capacity intelligent logistics at the endpoint (like the drone system in Factorio), but they do not provide high-capacity, full-end intelligent logistics like AE.

Of course, automation games often provide tools for manually building low-capacity endpoint intelligent logistics (such as the signal network in Factorio), but almost no one uses them to create endpoint intelligent logistics. All related attempts exist more as "good-looking toys".

If you want to enjoy playing this modpack, you should first abandon the on-demand design mindset and the concept of a central warehouse.

ftbquests.chapter_5DF8A114869675D1.quest: Some techniques for setting up stations were mentioned in
Page of Create

. Below are additional details not covered previously.

Due to the improvements by Apertyotis, the portable interfaces on the train are now only enabled when arriving at a station, so you no longer need to worry about issues like unintended interface connections!
Set Up Stations!
The standard design essentially involves forming the railways into a network, used for importing and exporting both items and fluids. The structures shown in the image are for demonstration only.
Standard Design

When you start experimenting with chemical industry, your production lines will become increasingly complex and involve more and more fluids.

At this point, you might realize that relying solely on belts and pipes for logistics is no longer sufficient — unless you have strong planning skills or are willing to make repeated refactors to complete your factory layout.

In this measure, I will provide a detailed guide on how to use trains to optimize your factory.
On the Train

The following explains junction design (assuming a standard one-way double-track railway with left and right lines).

There are two main types of railway junctions: crossings and switches (or interchanges).

A Crossing is simply where two rail lines intersect, without involving track switching. If you keep in mind that you're building in three-dimensional space, you can avoid the need for most crossings.

Our primary focus is on Switches. A switch is not merely an intersection; it also facilitate track changing and train reversal — allowing a train to move to another line or turn around on its current line.

Implementing this is not difficult. The key consideration is how to place signals to prevent collisions or deadlocks. (Signal placement techniques have been covered in Page of Create and won't be repeated here.)

Variations in switching methods and the number of possible directions give rise to various junction designs: roundabouts, T-junctions, etc. &eIn practice, there is no single "optimal" design — you should choose the most appropriate one for your specific scenario!&r
Monorail? Multirail?
Junction Design

Railway networks can be designed in many different ways.

The Bidirectional Single Track is the simplest: a single rail line where trains travel in both directions, shuttling back and forth. This design is inefficient, incompatible with multiple trains, and fails to leverage the flexibility of railways. It is only suitable for specific scenarios (e.g., transporting oil from a distant oil drill).

Next is the One-Way Loop: a single rail that forms a closed loop, with trains running in one direction, circling repeatedly. This design is also inefficient, prone to deadlocks, and not recommended for large-scale use.

The more common design is One-Way Multiple Tracks, where multiple parallel tracks are laid, each dedicated to one direction, connected at designated junctions. Only with this design can a true railway network be built, unlocking its full logistical potential.

&eFor railway bus construction, one-way double-track is typically the standard choice.&r
Monorail? Multirail?

Use the Train Schedule to define tasks for your train!

The train schedule allows the train to perform various actions in a specified order, and you can set completion conditions for each action individually!
When setting conditions, all conditions in a vertical column are AND (the entire column must be satisfied), while each column is connected by OR (if any column is fully satisfied).

When configuring logistics trains, the three most common conditions we use are Item Cargo Condition, Cargo Inactivity, and Scheduled Delay. Of course, you must decide how to use them based on the specific situation. Alternatively, you can refer to the following general-purpose configuration (not universal, but should work in most cases):

&e(Cargo Idle A sec) OR (Wait B sec) OR ((Item Count > C) AND (Wait D sec))&r
&ewhere A << D < B&r

&aWhy this setup? Consider the following four scenarios:&r
&61. Upstream buffer is ample — the train fills up quickly.&r
&62. Upstream buffer nearly fills the train, but production continues normally (no cargo idle).&r
&63. Upstream buffer is insufficient, but production is ongoing.&r
&64. Upstream has stopped production entirely.&r

&aThe goal of scheduling is to find the right balance between "ensuring logistics throughput" and "ensuring traffic efficiency".&r

&eFor Scenarios 1 and 4, we clearly want the train to depart as soon as possible. Here, the "Cargo Idle A sec" should apply.&r

&eFor Scenario 2, we also want a prompt departure. The condition "(Item Count > C) AND (Wait D sec)" should apply.&r

&eFor Scenario 3, we want the train to load as much as possible, but without waiting so long to cause a jam. &eIn this case, "Wait B sec" should apply.&r
Establish Standard

The term "Manhattan Layout" originates from urban planning. It can be thought of as a modular design: the factory is divided into individual, standard-sized modules (with identical or varied functions), surrounded by a standardized railway network.
Below is a fully realized example of a factory built using the Manhattan Layout:
Variant Design: The Manhattan Layout

In the measures "Factory Network" and "Page of Create," I have already discussed the concept of a bus. Now, it's time to use the train system to build a bus — &econsidering space and flexibility, I recommend using narrow tracks for construction!&r

Compared to belts and pipes, the greatest features of trains are their flexibility and adaptability. Additionally, trains can do logistics across vast distances.

No matter how complex your logistics needs are, you simply need to add stations to the bus and adjust the train schedules. The trains will then determine the routes and cargo status on their own!

&aYou should place the most frequently used materials into the train network, or even use the train network directly to transport all kinds of fluids between machines.&r

It's important to note that &ethe train bus doesn't necessarily have to connect directly to machines. You can also connect it to traditional belt buses, tank buses, and drawer buses&r — this can further reduce the number of stations and fundamentally minimize the possibility of deadlocks.
Railway Bus

To enhance train efficiency and prevent interference between production lines, it is recommended that you use dedicated trains for single item types in most scenarios.

Dedicated trains increase system stability, simplifies scheduling, and simplifies station design, making it a highly universal technique.

At the very least, you should assign dedicated trains for all commonly used fluids.

&eThere are numerous optional paths and branching content between different milestones. You can choose them based on your needs!&r

I Don‘t Know What to Do

Dirt can be multiplied through a simple loop!

2 Dirts + 2 Gravels = 4 Coarse Dirts

4 Coarse Dirts can be tilled with a hoe or mixed to become 4 Dirt, effectively doubling the dirt.

Alternatively, you can consider using Lava in contact with Saline Water to directly produce Coarse Dirt!

In the future, you can also use a similar method to quickly produce Mud and further produce Packet Mud, which can then be used in industry!

You can produce Cinder Flour by crushing Netherrack — and in the future, you can also use an Alloy Furnace.

Cinder flour can be filled with Lava to revert back into netherrack — or you can directly fill Cobblestone with lava to obtain netherrack.

You need cinder flour to produce Redstone, and further produce Glowstone Dust.

Of course, you can also produce them by washing crushed ore — though that is relatively less efficient.

You may notice that using Seed Oil or Ethanol to produce redstone is quite inefficient — while one bucket of Biodiesel can yield 40 redstone!
Tin is an essential material for many multiblocks, which is also used to craft Tin Hard Disks.
Check
Page of Metallurgy
for its production method. Click the underlined part to jump to it!
Preparation of Large Machinery

Salt can be obtained from Bone Meal!

You can use salt to produce Fries or prepare for further chemistry works!

At least for the current stage, I believe these two types of metal sheets should have automated production.

Many recipes require Iron Sheets, and you also need a lot of Copper Sheets for making pipes and tanks.

A very simple automated setup — such as a Mechanical Press and a Barrel — can meet most of your needs and save you a lot of time!
Metal Sheet

Cinder Flour filled with a small amount of fuel turns into Redstone!

In the early stages of your factory, your options are essentially limited to Seed Oil, Ethanol, Biodiesel, and Hydrogen.

Before electrolysis, producing hydrogen is very difficult (through water pyrolysis), so it can be ruled out first.

While seed oil and ethanol are simple, you'll find their demand is enormous — one bucket of seed oil only makes 8 redstone, and one bucket of ethanol only makes about 6.67 redstone!

Therefore, you should use biodiesel — one bucket of biodiesel can produce 40 redstone!

Alternatively, you can skip redstone production altogether — check out the Block Filling for Rose Quartz in Ponder!

Infinite Lava is one of the footstones of your industrial area!

It can produce an endless supply of stone, metal, Obsidian and Netherrack. Can also provide an infinite supply of regular heating fuel for Blaze Burners.

Build a 512-cubic-meter infinite lava pool to obtain unlimited fuel!

&eYou can build an infinite lava pool by utilizing the feature where flowing lava converts into a lava source block when those flows intersect (like water!).&r

(Recommended size: 8*8*8)
Refer to
Slimeli_'s Music Score
to check the list of fluids that can be infinitely extracted!
If you didn't know already, the underlined parts can be clicked to jump to the corresponding locations!

You need Kelp to make Mechanical Belts, Funnels, Tunnels, Hose Pulleys... they are all important components of your factory!

You can use a Mechanical Harvester to collect kelp, or use Rubber instead of Dried Kelp!

Seed Oil has a wide range of uses!

Besides serving as a lower-tier substitute for Lube Oil, producing Biodiesel, Redstone, and Biomass, it can also be used to make Crude Oil, or serve as a moderate fuel for Diesel Engines, and even fry Fries!

While there are multiple ways to produce it, you probably can't make a Brass Culture Bin or obtain Yeast right now, nor the Saline Water.

Thus, only two routes are available — using Mechanical Press to compact seeds or using Mechanical Mixer to heated mix seeds.

The mechanical press doesn't require heating but yields less.

The mechanical mixer requires heating but yields more.

Generally, I'd recommend heated mixing, but you can decide for yourself.

Cobblestone is the lifeblood of industry!

&eYou can easily obtain large quantities of cobblestone by mixing lava and water in a basin!&r

If you haven't done the math yet, the following data might help you:

&eA fully efficient Mechanical Mixer can produce approximately 76,800 cobblestone per hour!&r

Of course, the Andesite Casing needs to be mass-produced!

Before you can mass-produce Industrial Iron, the best solution is to use &eChip Wood Blocks&r and Andesite Alloy to craft it!

The Mechanical Core is the foundation for crafting various mechanical components.

For those commonly used mechanical components, it's best to automate their production — no need for high output, just having it is enough! This production model has a very interesting name: the Mall.

A Mall refers to integrating the production of various commonly used items into one place (&e efficiency is not the priority; full or semi-automation is sufficient&r) to form a relatively independent factory (or a black box). &a It does not supply other production lines but is solely for your manual use.&r The storage quantity of the products from such a factory is often limited to avoid excessive material consumption.

It‘s an efficient strategy to produce common construction components with this setup, while also generating essential crafting materials. &eThis can dramatically cut down on upfront material prep when constructing new lines!&r

For now, you should use Seed Oil and Ethanol to make Biodiesel — in the future, you might be able to use Gasoline instead of seed oil.

You have two ways to turn seed oil and ethanol into biodiesel — mixing or heated pressurizing.

Clearly, the heated pressurizing method can produce more biodiesel with fewer inputs.

Do you remember the output data of wheat plants? 2 Wheat Seeds and 1 Wheat!

Through crushing, the output becomes 3 Wheat Seeds and 1.5 Wheat Flour.

Using &eheated mixing&r for Seed Oil and &eFlour-Chip fermentation&r for Ethanol yields &a375 mB seed oil and 300 mB ethanol&r.

If you prioritize using these products to produce Biodiesel, there will still be a surplus of 75 mB seed oil that can be used to make other materials — but I don't recommend doing this.

By checking the JEI page, you can see that &e1B Biodiesel can provide 6 minutes of Super-Heated&r — this means that if you don't need to produce Glowstone or use biodiesel to produce Redstone, you don't require a very high biodiesel production rate for now! You can definitely use these raw materials for other purposes!
These metals are the footstone of factory construction — you'll definitely need to produce them in bulk!
Check
Page of Metallurgy
for its production method. Click the underlined part to jump to it!
Metal Production

You can obtain Sturdy Sheets from Obsidian.

There are many ways to produce obsidian —

Turn a Lava source into obsidian with Water.

Generate obsidian by having Cryogen come into contact with Lava.

Mix cryogen with lava to get obsidian.

Wash Magma Blocks to obtain obsidian.

You should easily be able to tell which methods are better or worse!

&aThanks to improvements in farming technique, farmland can no longer be trampled!&r
Seeds and agricultural products can be used to make Seed Oil, Ethanol, and Biomass.

&aAfter being improved, the Mechanical Harvester no longer consumes seeds when replanting!&r

I recommend using a &dSprinkler&r along with &dBonemeal Diluent&r to build a fully automated farm!
If you have interest, you can refer to the
Bone Meal
quest at right of this score, or simply click the underlined part to jump. (All underlined parts can be clicked for jump!)

In early game, compared to other crops, I recommend planting Wheat or Beetroot.

In the future, you can further advance to hydroponics using Nitrogen Fertilizer, and there might be more suitable crops then!

Without the &eFortune&r enchantment —
&a1 Wheat plant&r yields an average of &e2 Wheat Seeds&r + &e1 Wheat&r
&a1 Potato plant&r yields an average of &e3 Potatoes&r + &e0.02 Poisonous Potatoes&r
&a1 Beetroot plant&r yields an average of &e2 Beetroot Seeds&r + &e1 Beetroot&r
&a1 Carrot plant&r yields an average of &e2 Carrots&r

Crops have a growth stage of 0 when planted or after harvesting, and they mature when the growth stage reaches its maximum.  
Wheat, carrots, and potatoes have a maximum growth stage of 7; beetroot has a maximum growth stage of 3; for melons and pumpkins, after they mature, they produce fruit with a certain probability when selected by random ticks.

Silicon Sheet is an essential material for crafting Circuit Boards — besides that, you can also use it to make materials like Carborundum.

Its production is quite straightforward, so I won't go into detail here.

Amethyst is an important raw material in the electronics industry and can be used to make Silicon Sheets.

You can primarily obtain your first Amethyst Shard in three ways: 1. Mining it from Amethyst Geodes underground; 2. Mining Quartz Ore in the Nether; 3. Nether Quartz becoming Amethyst Shard through haunting.

&eYou can make it multiply by filling Budding Amethyst (a hidden recipe), and then use vibration to break down Amethyst Clusters.&r

Once you have unlimited Saline Water production, switch to the more efficient heated-pressurizing process to create Amethyst Clusters!

Additionally, it can also be used to produce Purple Dye or Nether Quartz.

&eCage&r can be used to keep chickens inside —
Chickens in cages become pure egg-laying machines!
&aUsing a Deployer to feed French Fries to a chicken in a cage will immediately produce an Egg!&r

Eggs can be used to make Sulphur and Bone Meal after being haunted into Rotten Eggs — of course, you can also use other methods to make them later.

Or you can simply eat them.

You have many options for producing Polished Rose Quartz!

If you start with Rose Quartz, you can choose Sand Paper or Belt Grinder — these are all viable routes available to you now!

The Belt Grinder is more compact, but requires controlling the RPM and is less efficient.

Sand Paper polishing is the fastest, but the setup is relatively larger.

In the future, you can use the more efficient Assembling Machine to replace them.

Quartz can be used to craft items such as Rose Quartz, &eNuggets of Experience&r, and more.

It can be obtained through methods like &ecrushing Amethyst&r, Quartz multiplication (by mixing with Lava), or washing Crushed Raw Gold.

Clearly, Amethyst is the best source.

The production of Sturdy Sheets is relatively simple — you don't need many of them for now.

In the future, you can use an Assembling Machine to produce them.

Sulfur can be used to produce Sulfur Dioxide, Sulfur Trioxide, and Sulfuric Acid, and can also be used to make Rubber. Sulfur dioxide can be used for hydroponics of Warped Fungus, Crimson Fungus and Nether Wart, and can further yield Gunpowder, and Dye.

In the future, it will be involved in numerous chemical recipes.

For you now, it can be used to produce sulfuric acid, which in turn can be used to make Ethylene!

However, this usage does not actually consume sulfuric acid, as the sulfur dioxide produced can be recycled to make sulfuric acid again!

Besides using Rotten Eggs, you can also automate sulfur using Scorchia. In the future, you will be able to use Methane (Natural Gas) or ore veins as well.

If you need to build a multiblock, then you obviously need a Hard Disk!

You don't need to automate its production for now!

&aYou can turn Bone Meal into Bones using a Mundane Potion to multiply Bone Meal&r!

Bone meal can be mixed with water to produce &dBonemeal Diluent&r, which can be used to boost growth of crops. &eCheck the Sprinkler's Ponder for details!&r

&aWhen producing bonemeal diluent, you can fully utilize the auto-output function of the Basin without needing a Smart Fluid Pipe!&r

Here is data on the number of growth stages for different crops. Crops mature at the final growth stage:

&aWheat&r has &a8&e growth stages&r
&aPotato&r has &a8&e growth stages&r
&aCarrot&r has &a8&e growth stages&r
&aBeetroot&r has &a4&e growth stages&r
If you have doubts about the efficiency of the Sprinkler, the next page will answer most of them — but I highly recommend thinking it through on your own!

First, we need to produce Bones, so let's start by looking at the recipe for making bones.

&eThe Fermentation Basin ferments for 4 seconds, consuming 50 mB of Mundane Potion to turn 3 Bone Meal into 3 Bones. 1 Bone can be turned into 4 Bone Meal via the Belt Grinder.&r

To make Mundane Potion, we need materials like Sugar, Redstone, and Blaze Powder. Here, we choose Sugar, which can be directly produced from Beetroot, as an example. &e1 Beetroot = 1 Sugar = 1,000 mB of Mundane Potion.&r

One Sprinkler consumes 500 mB of Bonemeal Diluent every 4 seconds to mature 24 crop blocks (increasing their growth stage by 1), meaning it produces 24 Beetroots in 12 seconds &e (because Beetroot has a total of 4 growth stages)&r. Thus, it produces 2 Beetroots = 2 Sugar = 2,000 mB of Mundane Potion per second.

In summary, the calculation shows: One Sprinkler Beetroot farm can supply 160 Fermentation Basins, producing 1,440 Bone Meal per second, which yields 105,000 mB of Bonemeal Diluent (without subtracting the Sprinkler's own consumption).

This means &aa net output of 104,875mB of Bonemeal Diluent per second, which can supply 859 Sprinklers to continuously mature 20,136 farmland blocks.&r

&aGenerally speaking, for each recipe of the same item, compared to other recipes, it can satisfy at most three of the following four conditions:&r
&61. High efficiency&r
&62. Easy to design&r
&63. Fewer materials&r
&64. Low tech requirements&r

&eIf a recipe satisfies all four... double-check your glasses!&r

&eWe choose recipes by weighing these four conditions against the intended item's characteristics.&r

Tech requirements are usually temporary, so we tend to ignore them. Typically, efficiency and easy design are our top priorities. However, if the raw materials are expensive, fewer materials may take precedence.

You can use this logic to formulate rules like: "If the slowest recipe is fast enough, ignore efficiency altogether."

&eOr, just prioritize what matters most to you. In a single-player experience, there‘s no "right" choice — only yours.&r
A Guide to Recipe Evaluation

In the early stages, you have two production methods for Circuit Boards to choose from:

&e1. Copper Sheet + Rose Quartz + Seed Oil&r

&e2. Brass Sheet + Polished Rose Quartz + Cryogen&r

The first route is simpler, but it requires more rose quartz and a large amount of seed oil.

The second route is more efficient, but it requires more other materials.

You don't necessarily need to achieve full automation for circuit boards right now; a semi-automatic line is sufficient for the time being!

If you wish to achieve full automation now, I think using the first route and obtaining rose quartz through block filling is a simpler choice! (Note that you don't need to pursue its production speed, as you would need about 40 fermentation basins to achieve its maximum efficiency with this recipe, and your current demand for it isn't actually that high)

Gravel can be obtained by crushing/milling Cobblestone.

Considering the efficiency (since you might need a lot of gravel!), you should choose to produce it via crushing!

Sand can be obtained by crushing Gravel.

Note that milling gravel does not produce sand; it produces Flint.

Blueprint Construction Station

Precision Mechanisms are likely the most complex component you can access now.

However, you won't need that many for now!

In the future, you can use the Construction Station to produce them quickly.

For the time being, the most significant use of Precision Mechanisms is crafting important components like the Lathe and Distillation Controller!

As for crafting materials, I recommend you also integrate &eIron Sheets, Copper Sheets, Sturdy Sheets, Bearings, Electric Gear Sets, and Circuit Boards&r into the mall.
